steps.title: Allocating heap memory
steps.explanation: We allocate space for one integer on the heap and store the address in pointer `p`.

steps.title: Storing a value in heap memory
Printing during memory usage
steps.explanation:
We print that the allocated memory is being used.

This is the valid usage period between malloc and free.

steps.title: Freeing heap memory
steps.explanation:
`free(p)` returns the heap memory, but does not erase the pointer variable itself.

After freeing, `p` becomes a dangling pointer, so use it with caution.

steps.title: Program termination
steps.explanation:
The program ends with `return 0;`.

Key point: malloc and free must be used as a matched pair (1:1).

quiz.question: What happens if you call free() on a stack variable (local variable) address?
quiz.explanation:
`free` can only handle addresses allocated by `malloc/calloc/realloc`.
Passing an invalid address confuses the memory manager and causes a program crash.

misconceptions.wrong: free(p) destroys the variable p itself
misconceptions.why:
It is just the 'house' that p pointed to that got demolished.
p still holds the address of the demolished house (Dangling Pointer).

keyTakeaway: Always return what you borrow with `free`. `malloc` and `free` are a pair.
